topic: Your GitHub is your first résumé (re-upload in the new style)

cover.concept: Retro tech still life: a beige 1990s computer and CRT on a wooden desk, its screen a soft grid of small green squares, a manila folder and floppy disks beside it.
cover.lineDraft: They open those before they read your résumé.

slides.label: First look
slides.idea: They see your six pinned repos first

slides.label: Step 1
slides.idea: A repo named after your username: four-line README (now, learning, open to summer 2027 internships, reach me)

slides.label: Step 2
slides.idea: Make each project runnable: screenshot, live link, three commands to run it

slides.label: Step 3
slides.idea: Pin three finished projects, not six copied tutorials

slides.label: The myth
slides.idea: Green squares aren't a score; nobody counts them, they open the repos

slides.label: Tonight
slides.idea: One hour tonight: username and photo, README repo, pin three projects, live link on each
friend who says "my GitHub is just a test repo"

images.name: cover
images.prompt: Photoreal retro tech still life, magazine-ad quality, warm natural light, subtle film grain. A beige 1990s desktop computer with a chunky CRT monitor on a worn wooden desk against a muted mustard-yellow wall; the screen glows with a soft grid of small green squares; a manila folder, two floppy disks and a coiled keyboard cable beside it. The subject sits in the lower 60% of the frame; the top 35% is plain empty wall. Portrait 2:3, natural colours. No readable text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no faces, no watermark.
